meta.game: Beneath the Mask - MBTI prediction party game
meta.authoring_rule: Every option is a miniature characterization of X: observational humour + affectionate roasting + plausible behavior. The joke is SURFACE ONLY. Weights are assigned from the underlying behavior the option describes, never from how funny or serious the option reads. funny != P, serious != J.

selection.shuffle_note: CRITICAL: option order must be re-shuffled per question per round, with the per-player answer mapping stored server-side. Fixed option order lets players memorize which option = which pole.

scoring.group_majority_correct: no bonus - group prediction feeds the 'how your group sees you' reveal only
scoring.winner: most total correct predictions across all rounds
scoring.tie_break: most best-predictor badges, then head-to-head correct answers

meta.type_derivation: Engine v2.6 (engine_v2_spec.md): normalized axis_fit (pole differences, sensitivity multipliers) + function_fit (0.25, derived via stacks) + duel_fit (0.10), softmax with tau; axis margins, confidence bands, closest alternatives stored per result. The bank stores EVIDENCE (w/fn/b); it does not compute types.

functions.role: SECONDARY RANKING LAYER (0.25 of candidate score via stacks). Axes remain PRIMARY (0.65); duels 0.10. Axis guard: a decided letter (axis margin > threshold) is never flipped by function or duel evidence — those reorder candidates WITHIN the axis skeleton only. Functions explain and narrow; they do not overrule the axes.
functions.anti_circularity: options carry behavioral constructs only. Function evidence is DERIVED from constructs via this table, never assigned directly to an option. An option therefore can never be its own evidence for a function.
functions.process: answer -> behavioral constructs -> behavior_to_function mapping (confidence-graded) -> function evidence profile -> reveal analysis

solitude-preference.note: do not over-read; primary evidence is the I axis

impulse-follow.note: generic P behavior; weak function evidence by design

flexibility-tolerance.note: generic P behavior; do not over-read

external-input-seeking.note: trust, Fe, and low confidence are all possible motives; none are observed

autonomous-decision-making.note: consults input, validates internally (owner correction, Q25-C)

functions.reveal_analyzer: when group type != self type: for each flipped axis, take questions where the majority vote != X's answer; collect the BEHAVIORAL constructs of X's actual picks vs the group's predicted picks; derive function evidence via behavior_to_function; render the disagreement in process language WITH its confidence ('the group read your behavior as systematic-execution (Te-leaning); your answers actually pattern possibility-exploration + values-driven-choice (Ne/Fi-leaning, moderate confidence)')

support_layers_future.big_five: future support layer: openness/extraversion/agreeableness/conscientiousness facets cross-check the axis profile
support_layers_future.enneagram: future support layer: motivational patterns cross-check the function profile
support_layers_future.rule: NEVER auto-override the MBTI result. On conflict, report it: 'INTP - moderate confidence; behavioral evidence partially conflicts'. The conflict itself is a feature: it drives the most interesting reveal moments.

functions.rule_v6: observable-behavior-first: text -> observable behavior -> construct(s) -> possible functions. No construct because it 'resembles' a function. No Fe because kind, no Ti because thinking, no Si because familiar, no Se because fast, no Ne because imaginative. If a response cannot distinguish functions -> non-diagnostic. One behavior may feed several functions. Some behaviors feed mainly the axes, not the functions.
functions.construct_vs_motive: a behavioral construct is NOT a psychological motive. Example: 'X asks five people before buying' OBSERVES external-input-seeking. It does NOT observe 'X trusts others', 'X is Fe', 'X lacks confidence', or 'X seeks harmony'. Those could explain the behavior; they are not observed. The dni field exists to block exactly these leaps.

option_schema.w: primary axis weights (with sensitivity multipliers); function and duel evidence refine ranking without overriding decided axes
option_schema.fn: DERIVED function evidence (from b via behavior_to_function; highest confidence per function wins). Never authored directly.
option_schema.dni: do-not-infer list: conclusions this option does NOT license
option_schema.alt: alternative non-MBTI explanations (context, habit, training, circumstance)

scoring_spec.authoritative: Axes PRIMARY (0.65, pole differences with sensitivity multipliers); function evidence SECONDARY (0.25, via stacks); duel evidence TERTIARY (0.10). Combined by softmax. No single layer is the sole estimator; the axis guard prevents silent letter flips. Uncalibrated weights throughout; promotion only by pilot data.
scoring_spec.confidence: margin between top-2 candidates, NOT a calibrated percentage. Displayed as the 'also suspected' list length, never as a % claim.

layers.A_family_probes: generate an initial NT/NF/ST/SF hypothesis only. Never declare a family from one scenario.
layers.B_duels: gather evidence distinguishing paired processes (Ni/Ne...). One selected option is never proof of a function.
layers.C_everyday: confirm/weaken the emerging profile with observable habits. Never overrides earlier evidence via axis stereotypes.

known_limits: cognitive functions are a hypothesis-generating model, not validated markers (stimulation-seeking != Se proof; systematic execution != Te proof)
12 questions cannot guarantee reliable identification; the game presents hypotheses with alternates, not diagnoses
score margins are uncalibrated until real response data exists

meta.coverage_note: Pure-random 12-draw coverage sim is DEPRECATED as a quality gate: item specialization (ambiguous options, zero-weight duel distractors) makes random draws miss axes by design. The production guarantee is the engine's constrained selection + coverage floor (engine_v2_spec section 3). Vitest must test the constrained selector, not pure random.
meta.scoring_labels: Wording doctrine: options with empty w are 'unscored by design' (decision documented in dni/alt), NEVER 'ambiguous'. The option text is precise and filmable; ambiguity was never the problem. The scorer declines to count the option toward typing — usually because confounds outnumber defensible readings. Prediction value is unaffected.
meta.interpretation_doctrine: EVERY option carries its interpretation in the 'b' field (behavioral construct) — no behavior is interpretation-free. Two layers, never confused: (1) interpretation = universal, the b construct says what the behavior IS; (2) axis scoring = selective, w says whether that construct links to an MBTI pole defensibly. An option can be fully interpreted (b) and unscored (w={}) — e.g. keeping the change = self-interest-prioritization: interpreted, but not an MBTI letter. The b field is also the bridge to future non-MBTI scoring (Big Five support layer).
meta.v96_note: Convergence round: four external architecture docs evaluated; doc4 (psychology-informed) ADOPTED as the reference mechanism — it independently restates this bank's doctrine (single answer = hypothesis not proof; ambiguous unscored; +1 uncalibrated start; process hypotheses separate from axes; no type from one item) and refutes the two overreach docs (full Jungian scoring = unfalsifiable; invented fractional weights = precision theater). SYNTHESIS: doc4 mechanism + bank voice. New adoptions: status lifecycle field; pilot protocol; player instructions; skip-without-penalty formalized; differential-effects review added to calibration policy.
pilot_protocol: Ask pilot players to EXPLAIN why they chose each answer; check they describe the intended distinction, not unrelated traits (kindness, confidence, competence)
Track ambiguous-option pick rates; flag options that attract people who intended the keyed answer
Check whether the SCENE wording (not the options) gives away the key
Test same-player consistency under option-order randomization (retest signal)
Review differential effects: occupation, culture, language, age, neurodivergence, prior MBTI familiarity
Never assign type from one item or a tiny sample; always confidence bands; playful profile, not verdict
Keep separate scores per hypothesized process; promote weights 1->2 only on pilot evidence (status: uncalibrated -> pilot_tested -> validated_for_game_use)

ROUTE-STABILITY TEST: for each pilot player, score 2-3 different valid 12-question routes; bank is stable only if different routes usually produce the same leading type or one of its closest alternatives (axis stability, top-type stability, margin, function-reveal stability). Random-coverage alone is necessary, not sufficient.
meta.player_instructions: Choose the option closest to what you would most naturally notice or do FIRST — before training, social pressure, role expectations, or deliberate correction. Answer for your TYPICAL reaction, not your ideal behavior. If two answers feel equally natural, pick the one you'd reach first with less effort. 'Both', 'neither', and 'context-dependent' are acceptable: skipping costs nothing. Option order is randomized; there is no 'A is better'.
meta.result_language: PREFER: 'Your answers were more consistent with converging on one explanation' / 'stronger tentative preference for pattern-convergence in these scenarios, alongside possibility-generation in others.' AVOID: 'You use Ni', 'this proves your type', 'definitely'. Functions are interpretive hypotheses, never verified dominant/auxiliary.
meta.context_sensitivity_rule: Constructs marked context_sensitivity:high get a 0.5 multiplier in engine scoring (moderate 0.75). Rationale: these constructs predict their pole only in some contexts (an extravert may need solitude after intense interaction; a P may plan when stakes are high). Weight and sensitivity are separate dimensions: weight = how much evidence, sensitivity = how context-dependent.
